A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VISTA3D research and contain complete, readable main text and supplementary material. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support comparison of all figures, tables, equations and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original supported-class, zero-shot and fine-tuning experiments in Sections 4–6, Tables 1–2 and Figure 3, plus supplementary quantitative results and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, numerical results and supplementary analyses, including the supported-class evaluations, zero-shot comparisons and fine-tuning results.

M1.justification: The shared SegResNet encoder, automatic and interactive branches, SAM-derived supervoxels, refinement algorithm and four-stage training procedure are unchanged, including supplementary training algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 11,454-scan CT collection, 127 supported classes, four external zero-shot datasets, mouse and WORD fine-tuning evaluations, and supplementary monkey CT example.

E2.justification: Corresponding supported-class and fine-tuning comparisons retain Auto3DSeg, nnUNet and TotalSegmentator. Zero-shot comparisons retain MedSAM and SegVol, and supplementary comparator participation is unchanged.

E3.justification: The 64%/16%/20% data splits, 128-cubic patches, sliding-window inference, Dice evaluation, simulated interaction procedures and fine-tuning sample counts are unchanged. No additional evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Figure 3 retains the same no-supervoxel ablation. Supplementary generalization examples, interactive correction cases, cross-slice responses and supported-class versus zero-shot embedding comparisons are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same average Dice reporting. There are no changes to repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty reporting or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Table 1 retains average Dice scores of 0.711, 0.760 and 0.792 for VISTA3D auto, point and auto+point; Table 2, Figure 3 and supplementary results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation in Section 3.2 and formal algorithm statements are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The revised abstract highlights editing automatic results, but this capability was already explicit in v1's introduction and method. Claims about automatic segmentation, zero-shot interaction and transfer learning retain their substantive scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations of supervoxel benefits, fine-tuning saturation and encoder/decoder sharing remain unchanged. Both versions retain the CT-only limitation and the difficulty segmenting large objects described in Section 7.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code-and-weights release and provides an early NVIDIA demo link. v2 replaces this with a statement that code and weights are available at the Project-MONAI/VISTA repository. Other implementation and reproducibility details are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and both reference lists are unchanged. The abstract rephrases the existing motivation without substantively changing novelty claims or positioning relative to prior segmentation methods.

P1.justification: The abstract is rewritten to clarify clinical motivation and summarize automatic segmentation, interactive editing and unseen-class annotation. This is a localized rewrite; the remaining prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised abstract produces minor text and spacing reflow on the first two pages, and the arXiv version/date stamps change. All figures, tables, captions and algorithm displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 provides a clearer abstract and replaces a future-release promise with a concrete repository reference for code and weights, modestly improving clarity and reproducibility guidance. Scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the improved access documentation, but do not verify the repository's contents.
